price.question: How much does a project cost?
price.answer: A landing page starts at {landingPrice}, an AI-ready site at {siteIaPrice}, an AI audit at {auditPrice} and an AI Sprint at {sprintPrice}. The final price depends on scope, which is agreed in writing before work starts. Every price is on the pricing page.

team.question: Who works on our project?
team.answer: Maxime Mansiet, our lead engineer, from the first call to the handover. He hands well-bounded tasks to AI coding agents, and the code they write is reviewed before it goes to production. If the project needs design or a specialty, we team up with a specialist and tell you first. The code is in your repo from day one, and every project ends with a written handover so another developer can pick it up. production.question: What do you mean by "in production"?

data.question: What happens to our data?

remote.question: Do you work with teams outside Bordeaux?

stack.question: What stack do you use?

agentVsAutomation.question: What's the difference between an AI agent and an automation?
agentVsAutomation.answer: An automation follows fixed rules: when an email arrives, it adds a row to the CRM. An AI agent reads, decides and acts within limits you set, for example sorting a customer request and drafting a reply. Many projects use both.

tools.question: n8n, Make or custom code?
tools.answer: It depends on the process and on who will maintain it. n8n or Make work well when your team wants to change the steps itself. Custom code makes sense when you need fine-grained control, tests or high volume.

nothingFound.question: What if the audit finds nothing useful?
nothingFound.answer: You keep the process map and the roadmap, even if you go no further.

pme.question: Is an AI audit useful for a 15-person company?
pme.answer: Yes, that is often where it pays back fastest. In a company of 10 to 50 people, a few repetitive tasks (quotes, invoices, follow-ups, email triage) take one or two people several hours a week. The audit finds them, puts a number on that time and checks that an automation costs less than what it saves.

duration.question: How long does the audit take?
duration.answer: One to two weeks between the first interview and the review. Interviews take about an hour per person, and we ask your team to show us their tools the way they really use them. The rest happens on our side: mapping, scoring the possible automations and writing the roadmap. You have nothing to prepare beforehand.

deliverable.question: What do I get at the end?
deliverable.answer: A written document, not a slide deck: the map of your processes, the possible automations scored by hours saved, cost and risk, the GDPR points to settle and a 90-day roadmap. We go through it together in the review meeting. It belongs to you, and you can hand it to another provider if you prefer.

bpifrance.question: Can your audit be funded by Bpifrance?
bpifrance.answer: Not this one. Bpifrance's Diagnostic Data IA goes through experts it accredits, and Klyx is not one of them. If that funding matters to you, talk to an accredited expert. If you want an answer within two weeks, at a fixed price and with no application to file, our private audit is built for that. TODO(maxime): check the terms on bpifrance.fr.

noTech.question: Do I need a tech team to follow the roadmap?
noTech.answer: No. Most of the small companies we work with have no in-house developer. We write the roadmap for the person who decides, without jargon, and each recommendation says who can carry it out: you with a tool like Make or n8n, us, or another provider. When a point needs real technical skills, we say so.

next.question: Do I have to hire you for what comes next?
next.answer: No. The audit is paid separately and the roadmap is yours. Part of the recommendations can often be done with the tools you already have. If you hire us for the next step, the audit price is deducted from the AI automation or the AI Sprint, depending on the project you choose. TODO(maxime): confirm the credit terms.

vsSprint.question: What is the difference between AI automation and the AI Sprint?
vsSprint.answer: AI automation is one linear workflow: a trigger, an AI step that reads or drafts, an action. The AI makes no decision on its own and the workflow does not connect five tools. As soon as the process needs to choose between several actions, or act across several tools with a test set, it is an AI Sprint, delivered in two weeks.

tools.question: Which tool does the workflow run in?
tools.answer: In your own n8n or Make account, in your name, so you stay in control. If you don't have a tool yet, we help you open an account, or install n8n on a server in your name. We also hand over the workflow export, which you can give to another provider. TODO(maxime): confirm the self-hosted n8n option.

runCost.question: How much does the workflow cost once it is live?
runCost.answer: You pay the vendors directly. Based on prices checked in October 2026, expect about €10 to €25 a month for an n8n server, around €30 for Make, and €20 to €80 of model API for a small volume. We give you an estimate for your case during scoping, before we start. TODO(maxime): check these ranges.

errors.question: What if the AI gets an invoice wrong?
errors.answer: That is planned for. We add a human approval step wherever a mistake is costly: the person sees the extracted fields, fixes them if needed and approves. The workflow also emails you when a run fails. Before launch, we test the AI step on 10 of your real documents to see where it gets things wrong.

data.question: Do my documents end up at OpenAI?
data.answer: The AI step sends the document's content to a model provider's API. By default, these business APIs are not used to train models. If your documents are sensitive, we pick a provider hosted in the EU or mask some fields before sending. We settle this during scoping, before the first step is written. whatIs.question: Is GEO just SEO for ChatGPT?
whatIs.answer: Partly. GEO stands for Generative Engine Optimization: the work that makes a site readable and citable by AI engines such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini or Google's AI Overviews. SEO aims for a rank in a list of links. GEO aims for a place among the few sources an AI engine cites in its answer. The two overlap a lot.

guarantee.question: Can you guarantee ChatGPT will cite me?
guarantee.answer: No, and nobody can honestly promise that. AI engines change their answers from one week to the next and do not publish their rules. What we commit to is the method: a baseline, documented fixes on your pages, and the same measurement at day 30 on the same questions. You see what moved, with the numbers to back it.

vsSeo.question: Should I stop doing classic SEO?
vsSeo.answer: No. AI engines rely largely on the same signals as Google: fast, well-structured pages with clear answers and verifiable facts. Good SEO is still the base. GEO adds direct answers at the top of the page, structured data, an llms.txt file and tracking of what AI engines say about you, question by question.

platforms.question: My site runs on WordPress or Webflow. Does that work?
platforms.answer: Yes. The offer is built for existing sites: WordPress, Webflow, Shopify or Next.js. We need editor access to change the 5 key pages and add the structured data. If your tool does not allow it, we hand over the copy and the markup ready to paste, and you publish them yourself. TODO(maxime): confirm the supported platforms.

citeme.question: How is this offer related to CiteMe?
citeme.answer: Maxime Mansiet, our lead engineer, co-founded CiteMe, a tool that measures how often a brand appears in AI engines' answers. We mention it because we use it for the measurements in this offer. You don't have to subscribe: the report, the tracked questions and the fixed pages belong to you, and you can run the tests yourself. TODO(maxime): confirm how CiteMe is used.

delay.question: How long before I see an effect?
delay.answer: The fixes are live within 2 weeks. Engines that search the web live, like Perplexity, can pick them up within days. Others rely on older data and take longer. That is why we run the test again at day 30, then every month if you take the GEO monitoring package.

problem.title: Tried ChatGPT, but nothing changed in how you work?
problem.body: That's true of most companies. In 2026, 40% of French small businesses use AI, but only 11% use it to automate a task (France Num 2026 barometer). That's what we do: we pick one task that takes time every week, automate it, and your team stays in control of what goes out to customers.
